author: manasjyotisharma
body:
## Problem
[CCDB-4880](https://confluentinc.atlassian.net/browse/CCDB-4880): Databricks Delta Lake Sink Connector sporadically fails with a NPE when trying to read "endOffset" tag from S3 objects. The root cause is that the Delta Lake Sink Connector under the hood leverages S3 Sink Connector code to write/create S3 objects and the S3 Sink Connector code in case of any tagging errors simply ignores them. However from Databricks Sink Connector POV ignoring such tagging errors means the S3 object is left in an inconsistent state because it expects that if object is there in S3 then tag must also be there for that S3 object. See discussions in this [slack thread](https://confluent.slack.com/archives/C011CCECDB7/p1660623278820309).

## Solution
Adding a S3 Sink Connector low level configuartion so that the client/caller can decide whether it is okay for it to ignore tagging errors or not. This PR is part-1 of a 2 parts PR. The part-2 PR will have the Databricks connector side of changes leveraging the newly added S3 Sink config & handle any tagging errors gracefully at Databricks Sink connector end. However until this current S3 Sink PR is merged and a new version is created, I cannot raise part-2 PR as in Databricks Sink Connector pom I'd have to use the new version number of S3 Sink Connector.

**PS:** Note that even though in the slack thread mentioned above, I mentioned about adding a retry logic, however that is already there within the S3 Sink code, see [S3Storage#newFullJitterRetryPolicy](https://github.com/confluentinc/kafka-connect-storage-cloud/blob/10.0.x/kafka-connect-s3/src/main/java/io/confluent/connect/s3/storage/S3Storage.java#L160) method. Since the [TopicPartitionWriter#tagFile](https://github.com/confluentinc/kafka-connect-storage-cloud/blob/10.0.x/kafka-connect-s3/src/main/java/io/confluent/connect/s3/TopicPartitionWriter.java#L658) method leverages an instance of S3Storage, so the S3 tagging error should have been retried 3 times with 200 ms exponential backoff (doubling each time). Since the original issue occurred sometime back, I am no longer able to grab the logs from Kibana/OpenSearch to verify whether that S3Storage retry logic got kicked in or not. However that aspect is not specific to the current Delta Lake issue and I'll leave it to the S3 Sink Connector owner to explore later in terms of general retry logic of S3Storage class implementation.

<!--- Mark x in the box. -->
##### Does this solution apply anywhere else?
- [x] yes
- [ ] no

##### If yes, where?
Databricks Delta Lake Sink Connector

## Test Strategy
Manually tested via docker playground the overall tagging failure scenario from Databricks connector end by hardcoding a throw clause in the S3 Sink Connector's TopicPartitionWriter#tagFile method.

<!--- Mark x in the box for all that apply. -->

- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests
- [ ] System tests
- [x] Manual tests

author: trabucayre
body:
Currently toolchains args are managed at targets level. This imply code dupplication and sometime missed args for a toolchain (for example with lattice nexus). FPGAs may have one toolchain (**ice40**, **efinix**), two (**ecp5**, **nexus**) or more (*xilinx* serie7 with **vivado**, **nextpnr** and **f4pga**).
This approach mean, when one wish to add a new toolchain for an existing device, an update must be done at **litex-boards** level to reflect alternate toolchain, with potential forget.

The idea of this PR is to add a two functions, at `build/xxx/platform.py` level, taking family model:
- first: fills argparse by calling all supported toolchain for family FPGAs and, when necessary, adds `toolchain` argument
- second: according to `family` and `toolchain` arguments fills the dict with corresponding values.

Thanks to that **targets** level is simplified because argparse is correctly filled transparently and all build/xxx updates will be automatically available at **litex-boards** level. This reduce redundancy because these task are written once and use everywhere and, finally, one wishing adding new toolchain (**apicula** or **mistral**) has to update these two functions instead of many **targets** files.

Unfortunately, since **toolchain** is only known after `args.parse` all toolchains args are shown instead of dedicated ones.

This PR isn't to be merge as it: once everyone are agrees with that I have to update all toolchains accordingly.

author: mikekistler
body:
This PR tries to unjumble the features exposed by the Cadl Http and Rest libraries.

The `@route` decorator is part of the Http library but was documented as part of the Rest library. I updated the README.md in the rest package to correct this.

I moved the `@autoRoute` decorator to the Rest library since it depends on the`@segment` decorator which is also in the Rest library. In this case I changed the code to match the documentation.

I also added a check in `$autoRoute` to ensure that no arguments were mistakenly specified, with a test for this.

And I made some small changes to the tests that should help catch decorators exported in the wrong library.

author: syntevoalex
body:
Previously, I already changed GTK build to treat warnings as errors, see Bug 570178

The commits come in reverse order: first, (not yet visible) warnings are fixed, and then strict `/W4` is enabled. This is so that each commit can be built successfully and there are no broken commits in the chain.

If you want to see the warnings being fixed (for review purposes), move the last commit to be the first. On the other hand, the nature of the warnings is rather evident from commits that fix them.

The patch set only targets Windows. Other platforms are only trivially affected by injecting new Windows-specific settings into all JNI native sources.

Noteworthy commits (all of them at the end):
* `Get rid of deprecated GetVersion()`
  Clears most of Windows version checks from SWT.
* `Deal with warnings about unreferenced parameters`
  Changes `JniGenerator` to inject warning settings into all generated sources.
* `Fix potentially uninitialized variable`
  That seems to be a good catch, where warning pointed to a potential JVM crash.

Fixes #369
